recent_posts.title: Mouth Coding
recent_posts.summary: Brad Frost introduces 'mouth coding' — a practice of verbally collaborating with an LLM in real time to build websites during live conversations. Using a real-world example of redesigning a small counseling practice's website with his wife, he outlines the key ingredients: live conversation, speech-to-text transcription, solid UI infrastructure, live preview, additional context, and human judgment. He argues this approach democratizes web creation, enables genuine cross-disciplinary collaboration, and is especially valuable for nonprofits and small organizations that lack dedicated web staff. The core thesis is that AI should facilitate human creativity rather than replace it, and mouth coding represents the most participatory, inclusive design process he's experienced in years.

recent_posts.title: Storybook MCP with Dominic Nguyen
recent_posts.summary: Dominic Nguyen, founder of Storybook and Chromatic, discusses the newly released Storybook MCP — a Model Context Protocol integration that lets AI generate UI features using existing design system components. A demo shows AI building a search feature, running it through Storybook's testing suite, and catching a real accessibility issue. The conversation covers the intersection of AI, design systems, and component-driven development, and promotes an AI & Design Systems course.

recent_posts.title: Coding Club
recent_posts.summary: Brad Frost visits his daughter's after-school coding club to share his passion for web development. He demos browser DevTools tricks on Minecraft's website, shows his daughter's vibe-coded game, and builds a live interactive webpage using JSON data collected from the kids in real time. The post reflects on the joy of sharing the magic of coding with children, free from professional jargon and business concerns.

recent_posts.title: AI as a creative infinite where anyone can make anything
recent_posts.summary: Brad Frost coins the term 'Creative Infinite' to describe AI as a fundamentally new creative medium — one where anyone who can articulate an idea can produce something from it with almost no friction. Using the example of his 8-year-old daughter vibe-coding a playable browser game in 5 minutes via Claude Cowork and Three.js, he argues that barriers to creation have fully eroded. He acknowledges AI's real concerns (IP, job displacement, misuse) but focuses on the unprecedented creative potential: inputs can be anything, outputs can be anything, and the process can be iterated indefinitely. He also notes that existing creative skills compound with AI rather than becoming obsolete.

recent_posts.title: How I redesigned my website using AI without touching a keyboard
recent_posts.summary: Brad Frost shares how he redesigned his personal website entirely hands-free using AI tools while painting a bathroom mural, describing it as a paradigm shift in creative workflow. He reflects on how AI removes traditional barriers between thought and creative output, and argues that foundational knowledge of design concepts and systems matters more than ever in this new era. The post concludes with promotion of his online courses covering AI & Design Systems, design tokens, and Atomic Design.

recent_posts.title: A Designer’s Thoughts About This Moment in AI
recent_posts.summary: Brad Frost shares a candid reflection on the tension designers and creators face in the current AI landscape. He criticizes the reckless commercialization of AI, particularly AI companies pursuing military contracts, while acknowledging that simply refusing to use AI is not realistic for most professionals. Using Michael Jackson as an analogy, he argues for holding two truths simultaneously: AI has genuine transformative potential for good, and the companies driving its development are behaving irresponsibly. His call to action centers on establishing personal and team values and principles to guide ethical use of AI, and recommitting to technology that serves the betterment of humanity.

recent_posts.title: Real-Time UI
recent_posts.summary: Brad Frost introduces the concept of 'Real-Time UI', where AI and design systems are used together to generate working UI prototypes live during meetings. The idea aims to make design more collaborative and participatory by lowering the barrier to creating digital interfaces, allowing teams to visualize and iterate on ideas in real time rather than spending meetings discussing abstract concepts. The post also promotes an upcoming AI & Design Systems course.

recent_posts.title: Fostering Community
recent_posts.summary: Brad Frost shares his vision for building a supportive community around his online courses. The community Slack includes channels for career development, advice, inspiration, music, pets, and other non-work topics. Access currently requires purchasing one of his courses on AI & Design Systems, Atomic Design, or Design Tokens, with plans to expand community offerings in the future.

recent_posts.title: Announcing Live AI & Design Systems Jam Sessions!
recent_posts.summary: Brad Frost, Ian, and TJ are launching biweekly live Zoom sessions starting February 26 for their AI & Design Systems course community. These jam sessions will feature demos, Q&A, community showcases, and discussions about integrating AI with design systems. The sessions are exclusive to course pre-orders and will be recorded for those who can't attend live.

recent_posts.title: Podcast episode with Christine Vallaure on work life balance and career autonomy
recent_posts.summary: A podcast episode featuring Christine Vallaure, founder of moonlearning and author of Solo, discussing work-life balance, autonomy, ambition versus competition, and finding fulfillment in the present rather than future goals. The conversation explores how to align personal values with professional pursuits and build a sustainable career as an independent creator.
